extracted.intended_audience: United States Indian Agents, Commissioner of Indian Affairs, and policymakers overseeing reservation administration
extracted.subtask_description: Standards and practical criteria for running Indian agencies/reservations in areas such as land and patent handling, agriculture, housing, schools, policing, health, missionary work, and trade enforcement. Drawn from annual agent reports with recommendations to the Commissioner.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provision of agricultural implements
rubrics_metrics.description: Encouragement in the way of agricultural implements is one of the chief necessities to bring Indians to husbandry.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If an Indian cannot procure necessary implements (wagon, harness, plow, harrow, etc.) after fencing a farm, he becomes discouraged and lapses to wandering life; therefore the agency should supply or facilitate access to implements to sustain new farmers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timely supply of garden seed and farm inputs
rubrics_metrics.description: Garden seed and other agricultural supplies must arrive in season to avoid total crop loss.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Late shipments (example: seed shipped in March arriving July) resulted in lost vegetable crops; ensure procurement and delivery schedules match planting seasons.

rubrics_metrics.name: Encourage and support Indian-built housing and infrastructure
rubrics_metrics.description: Facilitate and assist Indians in building homes and agency buildings, supplying carpentry help for doors/windows/floors while having Indians supply labor and materials when possible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide material, skilled assistance where necessary; example: Indians cut and hauled logs and erected 32 houses with minimal outside help; agency should continue to provide oversight and materials for further building.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide adequate agency buildings and service facilities
rubrics_metrics.description: Maintain and expand agency infrastructure (agent's house, warehouse, barn, saw-mill, blacksmith shop, schools, physician's dwelling) to meet reservation needs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Maintain stores of material and construct additional dwelling-houses and service buildings as population and needs increase; e.g., material on hand for two more houses should be used promptly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Promote and operate model government farms
rubrics_metrics.description: The government should farm land at agency sites to demonstrate agriculture and supply subsistence when needed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: government farms of 60 acres produced expected yields; government farming helps supplement rations during poor hunting seasons and provides demonstration plots.

rubrics_metrics.name: Allot land in sizes tied to labor and merit
rubrics_metrics.description: Divide available cultivated land into allotments (one-fourth to two acres in example) and award larger lots to the best workers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use allotment size as an incentive for industrious families; break additional land as needed to accommodate applicants.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prefer boarding schools where day schools fail due to mobility
rubrics_metrics.description: When children cannot consistently attend day schools because families move for hunting, boarding schools are the only feasible plan.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Submit plans/specifications/estimates for boarding-school buildings and obtain authority to erect them; boarding schools increase attendance and educational attainment (example: girls advanced from earlier boarding-school exposure).

rubrics_metrics.name: Separate boys' and girls' education facilities with vocational training
rubrics_metrics.description: Operate boarding schools in separate buildings with competent teachers and instruction in mechanical arts, mills, shops, and domestic skills.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide vocational instruction for boys (fields, mills, shops) and continued strong programs for girls; appoint competent supervisors (e.g., sisters of charity) to run schools.

rubrics_metrics.name: Maintain resident physician and sanitary oversight
rubrics_metrics.description: Keep a resident physician at the agency to treat disease and preserve sanitary conditions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Resident physician increases trust and reduces mortality; monitor outbreaks (e.g., measles) and report cases treated and deaths to Commissioner.

rubrics_metrics.name: Establish and staff mills, saw-mills and shops for local needs and apprenticeship
rubrics_metrics.description: Operate flouring and saw mills and blacksmith/carpen ter shops to provide services and apprenticeship opportunities for Indians.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide work where Indians deliver raw materials (logs, grain); accept that apprentices may prefer outdoors and require patience and forbearance to train effectively.

rubrics_metrics.name: Organize Indian police with chiefs’ participation and faithful leadership
rubrics_metrics.description: Create an Indian police force recruited by chief quotas and led by proven men of character.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Work with chiefs to supply men; select captains who have shown reformation and fidelity; police forces should be established and used when needed despite initial resistance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Restrict rations to rightful agency residents and prevent double-drawing
rubrics_metrics.description: Require tribes/individuals to decide a permanent home agency and abstain from issuing rations to those belonging to other agencies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prevent Indians from drawing rations at two agencies; maintain accurate rolls and refuse to issue rations where not justified.

rubrics_metrics.name: Enforce trade laws and suppress illicit trading (especially whisky)
rubrics_metrics.description: Actively prevent illicit trade by appointing deputy marshals and cooperating with law enforcement to apprehend traders, half-breeds, and unprincipled whites who traffic whisky.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Notify U.S. marshals and request sufficient officers (recommendation: three deputy marshals) to break up organized illicit trading networks; prosecution and arrests are necessary but may be difficult without resources.

rubrics_metrics.name: Coordinate with military to suppress horse-stealing and recover stolen stock
rubrics_metrics.description: Work with military commanders to take and return stolen stock to rightful owners and reduce horse-stealing, a major source of trouble.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When horses of white men are found in Indian possession, secure their return; where horses are stolen from other Indians, enforcement is culturally sensitive but necessary to break the custom.

rubrics_metrics.name: Require newcomers (conditional policy) to surrender arms/ponies and earn rations
rubrics_metrics.description: Treat certain incoming groups (example: Sitting Bull Indians) as prisoners of war requiring surrender of arms/ponies, and condition feeding on work in government service.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow Commissioner/Secretary instructions for handling large arrivals; record ponies and arms surrendered and place families on rations lists with work requirements to earn support.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use patience, explanation, and negotiation rather than force to resolve land disputes
rubrics_metrics.description: When chiefs refuse patents or object to changes (example: Bitter Root Valley patents), prefer commissions, conferences in Washington, and patient explanation of treaty terms rather than forcible removal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explain treaty articles and presidential orders carefully via interpreters; recommend sending a commission with authority or inviting chiefs to Washington to settle questions definitively.

rubrics_metrics.name: Deliver patents properly and take witnessed receipts after explanation
rubrics_metrics.description: When issuing patents to Indians, deliver them without unnecessary delay and take receipts properly witnessed, ensuring the Indians understand the implications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow prior instructions (cite: April 4, 1876) to deliver patents and obtain witnessed receipts, but ensure clear explanation of treaty consequences and implications for tribal relations and taxation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Encourage marketable labor and small-scale enterprise (e.g., wood and lumber sales)
rubrics_metrics.description: Promote activities that allow Indians to earn income by chopping and marketing wood, cutting lumber, and other marketable labor.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Support sawmills and markets so Indians can sell wood/lumber; example: 700 cords chopped with 300 marketed—such enterprises support transition to settled economy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Expand broken acreage through contracts to enable larger-scale farming
rubrics_metrics.description: Let contracts for breaking large tracts (example recommended: 300 acres) early so Indians can cultivate more land and increase agricultural production.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recommend contracting for land-breaking as soon as ground is suitable and obtain seed and resources to allow Indians to farm larger acreages next season.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adapt schooling strategy to seasonal mobility and hunting cycles
rubrics_metrics.description: Recognize that day schools fail where camps move seasonally; plan schooling (time and format) around hunting cycles and employ boarding where necessary.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Close or suspend day schools when camps move; where feasible, maintain winter school at stationary camps; record school costs and outcomes to justify boarding investments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Promote missionary and religious instruction consistent with social reforms
rubrics_metrics.description: Support missionary presence and church institutions which aid in forbidding polygamy, teaching respect for marriage relations, and providing moral instruction.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Permit and support missions (examples: Methodist, Presbyterian, Catholic) to provide regular services, Sabbath schools, and moral influence; use missions to promote social order.

rubrics_metrics.name: Maintain accurate health statistics and report major disease outbreaks
rubrics_metrics.description: Record number of cases treated by agency physician and deaths, and report outbreaks (measles, scrofulous diseases) to the Commissioner for action.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Track cases and mortality (example: 1,920 cases treated, 49 treated deaths, ~50 other deaths estimated) and use data to request medical supplies or interventions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Follow higher-level directives in communications with hostile or strategic Indigenous bands
rubrics_metrics.description: Abstain from independent negotiations or contacts with leaders (example: Sitting Bull) when instructed by the Commissioner/Secretary not to communicate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Adhere strictly to instructions to avoid undermining larger diplomatic/military strategies; reject peace offerings when policy forbids negotiation, but report any overtures to superiors.
